title: Swaraj Dweep and Shaheed Dweep (Batch 5)

places.summary: Home of Radhanagar Beach and the islands' best diving and snorkelling.
places.seoDescription: Plan a trip to Swaraj Dweep (Havelock Island): Radhanagar Beach, Elephant Beach snorkelling, diving, kayaking, sea walks and ferries from Sri Vijaya Puram.

overview.text:
Swaraj Dweep, called Havelock Island until December 2018, lies 41 km north-east of Sri Vijaya Puram in Ritchie's Archipelago and is the Andamans' main beach island. Its star is Radhanagar, Beach No. 7, on the west coast: Time called it the best beach in Asia in 2004, and it has held a Blue Flag for clean, safe and well-run beaches since 2020.

The island is also India's busiest dive centre, with many PADI and SSI schools and sites such as Dixon's Pinnacle. Snorkellers head to Elephant Beach, and there are kayaking trips through the mangroves, some at night to see bioluminescence, and helmet sea walks. Ferries, both government boats and private catamarans, link it to the capital and to Neil. Saltwater crocodiles live in these waters, so swim only where it's allowed.

overview.text:
Shaheed Dweep, called Neil Island until December 2018, lies about 36 km north-east of Sri Vijaya Puram, between Havelock and Rose Island. It was uninhabited until settlers arrived in the late 1960s, and today about 3,000 people live in five villages. It's a flat farming island that grows vegetables and organic produce for the rest of the Andamans, with very little traffic and a slow pace.

Each beach has its own character: shallow Bharatpur and Sitapur for swimming and sunsets, and Laxmanpur, which faces the sunset, and the limestone Natural Bridge, best seen at low tide. Reefs lie just offshore for snorkelling and low-tide reef walks. Seafood is caught daily by local fishermen. Ferries stop at Neil Kendra jetty from the capital and Havelock, so it slots easily between the two.
